author: ojiudezue
title: Registry, never name guessing: resolve platform, NVR family, device, person and room from HA registries, not entity-id strings
summary: The house-wide sweep found 171 raw hits, ~45 decision sites, and two live bugs the guesses were hiding: the HVAC fan-off-while-occupied guard silently off in 10 of 47 rooms (binary_sensor.foyer_occupied 404 vs foyer_foyer_occupied 200), and Oji's 14 iphone_oji_* Bermuda sensors never found because code searched oji_udezue. The garage_a _2 Frigate camera was never paired with its Protect twin, so its crossings never earned two-NVR confidence.
why: Operator rule after learning perimeter and census still guessed Frigate vs Protect from entity-name suffixes: 'Unacceptable to do the latter anymore. It's invalidated [whole] features in the past.' Now in CLAUDE.md; a new name guess is a defect.
implications: Every future plan, build and review must cite a registry lookup for identity; a CI guard (AST scan, shrinking allowlist with owner card) will fail new guesses. Frigate devices carry no MAC, so cross-NVR pairing needs one explicit resolver, not a pure registry fact.

alternatives_considered.option: Fix each guess when it bites
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: it already invalidated whole features (music following person filter, AI rule person filter, garage_a pairing) before anyone noticed

alternatives_considered.option: Ask the operator to rename entities to match conventions
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: renames ripple through every list and do not help another install; names are not identity

revisit_trigger: If a registry lookup proves impossible for a class of entity (e.g. Frigate pairing), the logged-and-counted fallback must stay at zero live hits; a non-zero counter reopens the design.
